title: JavaScript errors, exceptions, and error objects
concepts: Distinguishing language errors from host-defined diagnostics

sourceSnapshot.authority: ECMA-262, Web IDL, and MDN JavaScript reference

accuracyFacts: ECMAScript 2026 adds Error.isError. It checks the internal ErrorData brand, so it accepts genuine cross-realm ECMAScript errors and rejects objects that only inherit Error.prototype; a Proxy wrapping an Error does not itself carry the target's internal slot.

Error.isError is a current standard API but MDN marks it as limited availability; separate language-standard status from support in a particular browser/runtime and feature-detect when targeting unpinned engines.

Error, NativeError, and AggregateError constructors can be called without new. Error options cause creates an own non-enumerable data property only when options has a cause property, even when its value is undefined.

AggregateError consumes its errors argument as a synchronous iterable during construction and stores a new array on a writable, non-enumerable, configurable own errors property. Its message and optional cause have their own error-property rules.

The standard EvalError type remains for compatibility but is not currently produced by the ECMAScript specification. Runtime messages, stack formatting, and stack properties are host-specific rather than portable ECMA-262 guarantees.

The throw statement throws any ECMAScript value, not only Error instances. Catch receives that exact value; robust boundaries may normalize non-Error thrown values while preserving them as cause or metadata.

A finally block always runs as control leaves try/catch. A normal completion preserves the prior completion, while an abrupt completion in finally (return, throw, break, or continue) replaces it and can suppress a pending exception or return.
A synchronous try/catch does not catch a Promise rejection that occurs after control leaves the try. In async code, await the promise inside the try to catch its rejection there.

Error.prototype.toString dynamically reads name and message, stringifies them, uses defaults only for undefined, returns only the message when name is empty, and otherwise combines name and message with colon-space.

Error subclass constructors should call super(message, options) to initialize the ECMAScript Error brand and cause behavior before using the instance; runtime stack capture and formatting remain host-specific.
